name: Pinnacle West Capital

logo.source: en.wikipedia.org infobox logo (Pinnacle West Capital logo.png)

description: Pinnacle West is a holding company that derives essentially all of its revenue and earnings from Arizona Public Service (APS), the regulated electric utility serving about 1.4 million customers in Arizona. APS owns or leases 6,257 MW of regulated generation (nuclear, gas, coal, solar) and buys more under long-term contracts; the Arizona Corporation Commission (ACC) sets rates to recover cost plus a return (9.55% ROE in the current order, 10.70% requested in the pending case). About 95% of revenue is retail electricity, split evenly between homes and businesses, and growth comes from customer growth in the Phoenix area and rate-base investment.

gics.note: Conventional filing label: GICS Sector 'Utilities' and Sub-Industry 'Multi-Utilities' per Wikipedia 'List of S&P 500 companies' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_S%26P_500_companies, read 2026-09-30). That list gives only Sector and Sub-Industry. SEC SIC code 4911 (Electric Services) per EDGAR. Despite the Multi-Utilities label, the 10-K says essentially all revenue and earnings come from one electric utility, APS.

employees.note: Pinnacle West 94, APS 6,516; the APS figure includes about 2,400 employees at jointly owned plants that APS operates; about 1,120 APS employees are IBEW union members (FY2025 10-K)

businessLines.name: Regulated Electricity (APS)
businessLines.how: Customers pay ACC-approved retail tariffs monthly based on usage; fuel and purchased power ($1,933M in 2025) are recovered through adjustors, and profit is the allowed return on rate base (original-cost rate base plus a 1% return on the fair-value increment under Arizona law), so earnings grow with customer growth and capital invested.
businessLines.description: Generation, transmission and distribution of electricity to about 1.4 million customers in Arizona under traditional cost-based regulation; the only reportable segment.

revenue.note: Segment operating revenues; FY2024 $5,125M; FY2023 $4,696M. By class: residential $2,541.3M (47.6%), non-residential $2,542.9M (47.6%), wholesale $108.7M (2.0%), transmission for others $129.7M (2.4%), other $17.4M (0.3%) (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/764622/000076462226000011/pnw-20251231.htm)
